security_properties.property: BLSToExecutionChange messages MUST be cryptographically signed with the validator's BLS key before submission to community repository
security_properties.rationale: Unsigned or incorrectly signed messages could allow attackers to claim withdrawal credentials without proving validator ownership

security_properties.property: Community signature verification MUST validate BLS signature over the complete withdrawal change parameters before acceptance
security_properties.rationale: Incomplete verification could allow tampered messages to enter the broadcast file, potentially redirecting validator withdrawals

security_properties.property: Beacon nodes MUST have broadcast file loaded BEFORE Capella fork activation to provide protection
security_properties.rationale: Late loading creates a window where attackers can race legitimate messages at fork activation

security_properties.property: All messages in broadcast file MUST be transmitted exactly once at Capella activation
security_properties.rationale: Missing broadcasts leave validators unprotected; duplicate broadcasts waste network resources

security_properties.property: External validator submissions MUST NOT bypass the community verification process
security_properties.rationale: Direct inclusion without verification could allow attackers to inject malicious claims

security_properties.property: Claim filename MUST match validatorIndex.json format with valid numeric index before any signature verification
security_properties.rationale: Malformed filenames could enable directory traversal or index confusion attacks

security_properties.property: Validator index MUST correspond to an active validator on the beacon chain consensus layer
security_properties.rationale: Claims for non-existent or inactive validators could be accepted and later conflict with legitimate validators

security_properties.property: Only ONE BLSToExecutionChange operation SHALL be accepted per validator index in the broadcast file
security_properties.rationale: Multiple operations per validator could create conflicting withdrawal credentials or enable double-claim attacks

security_properties.property: Claims that fail any validation check MUST be rejected and MUST NOT enter the broadcast file
security_properties.rationale: Partially validated claims could compromise the integrity of the broadcast file protection mechanism

security_properties.property: External claim submitters MUST NOT be able to modify claims after BLS signature verification
security_properties.rationale: Post-verification modification could redirect withdrawal credentials without valid cryptographic proof

security_properties.property: Messages that conflict with broadcast file entries MUST be rejected and dropped, never propagated
security_properties.rationale: Propagating conflicting messages assists attackers in racing legitimate withdrawal credential changes

security_properties.property: Messages matching broadcast file signatures MUST be accepted and propagated normally
security_properties.rationale: Blocking legitimate messages would prevent rightful withdrawal credential changes

security_properties.property: P2P peer messages MUST be compared against local broadcast file before acceptance or propagation
security_properties.rationale: Accepting messages without filtering defeats the protection mechanism against compromised deposit key attacks

security_properties.property: Messages for validators without broadcast file entries SHALL be accepted (no preferential filtering)
security_properties.rationale: Validators who didn't pre-submit claims should still be able to submit withdrawal credential changes

security_properties.property: Contested claims where on-chain data cannot prove ownership MUST require out-of-band social consensus resolution
security_properties.rationale: The protocol cannot cryptographically resolve ownership disputes when attacker controls deposit key (AMB-EIP4736-01)

security_properties.property: Protection effectiveness REQUIRES widespread node operator participation in loading broadcast files
security_properties.rationale: Without sufficient adoption, attackers can propagate conflicting messages through non-filtering nodes (ASSUM-EIP4736-01)

security_properties.property: BLOBBASEFEE opcode (0x4a) MUST push the current block's blob base fee as a left-padded 32-byte value onto the stack
security_properties.rationale: Incorrect value format could cause smart contract calculations to fail or produce wrong results

security_properties.property: BLOBBASEFEE MUST read blob gas price using get_blob_gasprice(header) as defined in EIP-4844
security_properties.rationale: Using wrong calculation method could return incorrect blob fees affecting rollup cost calculations

security_properties.property: BLOBBASEFEE execution MUST deduct exactly 2 gas units
security_properties.rationale: Incorrect gas charging could enable spam attacks or make the opcode unusable for cost tracking

security_properties.property: BLOBBASEFEE execution MUST verify at least 2 gas remains before operation
security_properties.rationale: Executing without sufficient gas violates EVM gas accounting invariants

security_properties.property: BLOBBASEFEE with insufficient gas MUST revert with out-of-gas error
security_properties.rationale: Proceeding despite OOG would violate EVM execution model and enable gas-free operations

security_properties.property: Gas cost for BLOBBASEFEE MUST be fixed at 2, matching BASEFEE opcode cost
security_properties.rationale: Variable costs could enable timing attacks or break contract assumptions about execution cost

security_properties.property: Rollup contracts MUST be able to trustlessly access current blob base fee via BLOBBASEFEE opcode
security_properties.rationale: Without trustless access, rollups cannot accurately price L2 transactions for L1 data availability costs

security_properties.property: L2 fee adjustments based on BLOBBASEFEE MUST reflect actual L1 blob data costs
security_properties.rationale: Inaccurate fee adjustment could cause rollup operators to lose funds or overcharge users

security_properties.property: BLOBBASEFEE MUST only be valid on chains/blocks with EIP-4844 enabled, reverting with invalid opcode otherwise
security_properties.rationale: Behavior on non-4844 chains is unspecified and could cause undefined behavior (AMB-EIP7516-01)

security_properties.property: Blob base fee value in header MUST accurately reflect actual blob gas market conditions
security_properties.rationale: Manipulated blob fees could cause rollups to under/over-charge users for data availability (ASSUM-EIP7516-02)

security_properties.property: Push operation MUST increase stack size by exactly 1 and place value at top
security_properties.rationale: Incorrect stack modification could corrupt execution state and break contract logic

security_properties.property: Pop operation MUST decrease stack size by exactly 1 and return the top element
security_properties.rationale: Incorrect pop behavior could leave orphaned values or return wrong data to operations

security_properties.property: Stack size MUST be checked against 1024 limit BEFORE any push operation
security_properties.rationale: Post-push overflow check could corrupt memory beyond stack bounds

security_properties.property: Push to stack with len(stack) == 1024 MUST raise StackOverflowError immediately
security_properties.rationale: Allowing overflow could cause memory corruption or buffer overflows in EVM implementations

security_properties.property: Stack size MUST NEVER exceed 1024 elements under any operation sequence
security_properties.rationale: Exceeding limit would violate EVM specification and could enable memory safety exploits

security_properties.property: Stack MUST have len(stack) > 0 BEFORE any pop operation
security_properties.rationale: Popping from empty stack would return undefined data potentially from previous executions

security_properties.property: Pop from stack with len(stack) == 0 MUST raise StackUnderflowError immediately
security_properties.rationale: Proceeding with empty pop could return garbage data and break contract execution

security_properties.property: Stack underflow errors MUST halt execution, not silently continue
security_properties.rationale: Silent continuation could mask bugs and enable undefined behavior exploitation

security_properties.property: Stack MUST have sufficient elements for opcode inputs BEFORE execution
security_properties.rationale: Executing with insufficient inputs would pop undefined data

security_properties.property: Stack MUST have sufficient space for opcode outputs after inputs consumed
security_properties.rationale: Executing without output space would cause overflow on push

security_properties.property: Opcodes with failed stack validation MUST NOT execute, transitioning directly to error state
security_properties.rationale: Partial execution after validation failure could corrupt state

security_properties.property: Opcode execution SHALL only proceed after validation passes
security_properties.rationale: Executing before validation could cause undefined behavior

security_properties.property: StackOverflowError and StackUnderflowError MUST cause immediate execution halt with all gas consumed
security_properties.rationale: Error handling behavior not fully specified; consistent with other EVM execution errors (AMB-CANCUN-STACK-02)

security_properties.property: Stack operations MUST be atomic and MUST NOT be subject to race conditions
security_properties.rationale: Non-atomic operations could corrupt stack in concurrent scenarios (ASSUM-CANCUN-STACK-01)

security_properties.property: Stack bounds checks MUST NOT be bypassable through any combination of opcodes
security_properties.rationale: Bypassing bounds checks could enable stack corruption and arbitrary code execution (ASSUM-CANCUN-STACK-02)

security_properties.property: All U256 values MUST be stored and retrieved from stack without loss or corruption
security_properties.rationale: Value truncation would break contract execution correctness (ASSUM-CANCUN-STACK-03)

security_properties.property: Stack MUST maintain LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) ordering for all operations
security_properties.rationale: Violating LIFO would break EVM execution model and all stack-based operations

security_properties.property: Stack state MUST be deterministic given the same initial state and operation sequence
security_properties.rationale: Non-determinism would break consensus and enable state divergence between nodes
